scope: Roadmap item 3, identification half: what the packaged ARM64EC DXVK/VKD3D actually are, and what they require.
method: Downloaded the exact three components Prepare Vapor installs (VaporPreparation.kt URLs), extracted, and read PE version resources, embedded version strings, git revisions and Vulkan symbol strings from the shipped DLLs.

DXVK-1.10.3-arm64ec-async.wcp.revision_note: not found in upstream doitsujin/dxvk; the gplasync fork is not reachable. The build is from an ARM64EC port whose source is not publicly locatable.
DXVK-1.10.3-arm64ec-async.wcp.license: zlib/libpng (its own version resource says so; text bundled as licenses/dxvk-zlib-libpng-LICENSE.txt)
DXVK-1.10.3-arm64ec-async.wcp.build_state: UNSTRIPPED - about 10x the size of the 2.7.1 build (d3d11.dll 41.6 MB vs 4.0 MB)

DXVK-2.7.1-arm64ec-gplasync.wcp.note: contains vkd3d-proton and D3D11On12CreateDevice strings, so it is built from a Proton-family tree

VKD3D-3.0.1-arm64ec.wcp.identity_evidence: d3d12.dll contains the message "vkd3d-proton d3d12core interfaces"; both DLLs carry VKD3D_CONFIG/VKD3D_DEBUG env names
VKD3D-3.0.1-arm64ec.wcp.layout: d3d12.dll is a small loader that delegates to d3d12core.dll

findings: Both DXVK builds deliberately spoof their Windows version resources (10.0.17763.1 WinBuild.160101.0800), so PE version resources cannot identify them. The embedded "DXVK vX.Y.Z" string is the real marker.
Both are unofficial async builds (arm64ec-async and gplasync), not stock DXVK releases.
DXVK 1.10.3 is unstripped - its d3d11.dll is 41.6 MB against 2.7.1s 4.0 MB. That is 10x the disk and a larger mapping cost at load, for no functional gain.
Only DXVK 1.10.3 embeds a source revision, and it does not resolve in the public dxvk repositories.
vkd3d-proton 3.0.1 carries no version resource and no revision at all.
open: map the 2.7.1-gplasync and vkd3d-proton 3.0.1 builds to source (no revision is embedded)
the measurement half of roadmap item 3 (submission cost, shader stalls, waits, memory, cold/warm) needs a GPU and remains physical-hardware work
